sunset-house.blurb: Five-bedroom villa in La Santa María, facing west over the bay of San Juan del Sur. Sleeps ten, 4.5 baths, private pool, A/C in every room, generator and cistern. The terrace is the point: the sailfish on the wall, the glass railing and the Pacific turning to gold.
sunset-house.tip: The town is five minutes away, down the hill. Villa guests can use the resort's pool, gym, clubhouse and coworking.

amenities.label: Infinity pool
amenities.detail: Open 7:00–21:00. Bay view, loungers, a cabana and a bar. The sunset drink is taken on the terrace.

amenities.label: Gym and yoga
amenities.detail: Treadmills, bikes, ellipticals and weights. Group yoga and a trainer on request. Peloton bikes in the gym.

amenities.label: Coworking
amenities.detail: Fiber wifi, air conditioning and tables overlooking the pool and the bay. The room for working.

amenities.label: Clubhouse

amenities.label: Snacks and smoothies

amenities.label: Courts

amenities.label: 24/7 concierge
amenities.detail: Tours, transfers, reservations and wellness. Gated entrance with security all day.

lsm.blurb: Hotel and residences on the hill above San Juan del Sur. Infinity pool facing the bay, gym and yoga, fiber-internet coworking, clubhouse, snack bar, courts and a pirate-ship playground. Gatehouse, 24/7 concierge, five minutes from town.
lsm.tip: Tap each amenity. Sunset Home Villa #2 is the five-bedroom villa on the hill.

el-caite.tagline: Orange building, a block from the market

hotel-cascada.blurb: South of the municipal cemetery, 1.2 km from the center. A pool with a real waterfall, garden, grill, terrace, rooms with A/C or fan. Parking and 24-hour security. The quiet getaway when you want water without a resort price.
hotel-cascada.tip: South side of the San Pablo municipal cemetery. Beach about a 15-minute walk. Cash payment on arrival. No breakfast.

amenities.label: Piscina con cascada
amenities.detail: Piscina al aire libre con cascada. Por esto se queda aquí: agua, sin precio de resort. Los cuartos miran a la piscina.

amenities.label: Jardín y terraza
amenities.detail: Jardín alrededor de la piscina, terraza y sala compartida. Tranquilo, al sur del cementerio.

amenities.label: Asador
amenities.detail: Área de asado para huéspedes. Lleva la carne: aquí no hay restaurante.

amenities.label: Habitaciones
amenities.detail: Cuartos con ventilador o aire. Baño privado y agua caliente. Algunas unidades tienen sala o comedor.

amenities.label: Cocina
amenities.detail: Privada o compartida, según el cuarto. Microondas, horno y tostadora. Pregunta cuál te toca antes de reservar.

amenities.label: Wifi
amenities.detail: Wifi gratis en la propiedad.

amenities.label: Parqueo
amenities.detail: Parqueo privado gratis dentro de la propiedad.

amenities.label: Seguridad
amenities.detail: Seguridad las 24 horas. Recepción 6:00–23:00. Check-in 11:00–23:00, check-out antes de las 12:00. Sin toque de queda.

el-pacifico.tagline: Pool two blocks from the beach
el-pacifico.blurb: Hotel in La Talanguera, two blocks from the beach and a ten-minute walk along the sand to the center. Fruit-tree garden, big pool and a free shuttle from Casa Oro Eco Hostel; rooms from US$35.

la-estacion.blurb: Family-run boutique hotel with 18 rooms in the heart of the port, steps from the sea, founded by doña Guadalupe Morales. Its restaurant El Buen Gusto, serving Nica food and seafood, sits right on the main beach.

hulakai.blurb: Hotel on a hill about 500 m east of Playa Maderas, with ocean-view rooms, a pool with a bar and yoga. The walk down to the beach is short but steep.

dreamsea.blurb: Eco surf camp in the forest near Marsella: a three-story bamboo main building with a restaurant, bar and yoga on top, and ten raised cabins across dorms, twins and suites. Pool with a bar, surf lessons and yoga.

clandestino.tagline: Surf hostel with a skate bowl
clandestino.blurb: Surf hostel a few minutes' walk from Playa Maderas, with jungle cabins, its own concrete skate bowl and a yoga deck. Dorms from US$15 and private rooms from US$40.

socialtel-maderas.blurb: The former Selina Maderas, 200 m north of the Marsella junction and a few minutes' walk from the beach. Dorms, tipis and suites around the pool, with a restaurant, yoga deck and coworking.

verdad.blurb: Boutique hotel and retreat on Playa Escameca, south of town: five little houses with ocean views and two rooms by the pool. Surf school, open-air yoga studio and transfers from Managua or Liberia.

viyarte.blurb: Boutique hotel and retreat center five minutes from Playa Marsella, next to Maderas. Rooms with A/C and hot water, a pool, a restaurant and a yoga space with an ocean view.

casa-de-olas.tagline: Eco hostel with an infinity pool
casa-de-olas.blurb: Adults-only hostel on a hill about 3 km from town, with a pool, hammocks and the sunset over the bay. Breakfast included, shared kitchen and a free shuttle to town; no air conditioning.

mango-rosa.blurb: Twelve units on seven acres of garden, four minutes by car from Playa Marsella and eight from Maderas. One-bedroom bungalows and two-bedroom ranchers with a kitchen and A/C, a pool and a restaurant.

hush-maderas.tagline: Eco lodge with an infinity pool
hush-maderas.blurb: Eco lodge a five-minute walk from Playa Maderas, almost entirely solar-powered. Infinity pool with a 180° ocean view, yoga studio, rooftop for the sunset and breakfast included.

buena-vista-surf.blurb: Eco lodge of six wooden cabins in the jungle above Playa Maderas, with an infinity deck among the trees for yoga and sunsets. Surf packages and dinners by Nica chefs; no A/C, just fans.

jose-sevilla.blurb: The seafood counter and table. Soup, fish in cream sauce with shrimp, tostones. The home of Esterlina Sevilla Alvarado: first the fish market, then the plate.

arenas-pizza.tagline: Pizza at the port food park

ka-nuk.tagline: Food cart across from Tio Milton

dockside.tagline: Tacos with a view of the port

vickys-pizza.blurb: San Juan-style pizza delivered to your door, free delivery. Thick, oven-baked crust: ham, pepperoni, chicken, creole chorizo, Hawaiian, vegetarian, jalapeño, mushroom or mixed. Red sauce or pesto, and a cheese crust if you like. Personal C$240, medium C$330, family C$370, extra-family C$470. With cheese crust, C$300 to C$600.

rusti-k.tagline: Local buffet, 50 m from the UNO

sunny-beach.tip: From Rest. El Timón, 200 m north, on the beachfront. Instagram @sunnybeachbar.

rincon-maria.blurb: Green-walled comedor in San Juan del Sur. The name is hand-painted: El Rincón de María, Sazón Leones. The sidewalk chalkboard announces lunch for C$100, fresco included. Rice, beans, plantain slices and the stew of the day.
rincon-maria.tip: The price is on the chalkboard. Ask about the fresco of the day.

social.tagline: Pool, wings, 1 block from the UNO

barillas-express.tip: WhatsApp +505 8159-6777. North side of the roundabout.

playa-sjds.blurb: The half-moon you came for. Boats on the sand, the malecón, the Cristo on the south hill and a sunset that stops traffic. Don't swim in the morning; walk the beach as the sun goes down. This is the town beach. Everything else is a taxi ride.

astillero.tagline: The end of the coastal road

vivian-noche.blurb: The port's palapa when there's a band: live music Friday through Sunday, a full bar and the bay a few steps away. Seafood if you're still hungry. The local night out, no cover.

surf.tagline: By the day or the week

pali.blurb: The Walmart supermarket by the bridge, in barrio Las Pampas. Rice, beans, chicken, vegetables, beer, cleaning supplies: the cheapest full shop in town. Full aisles, cards accepted. Stock up here and buy fruit at Guevara.

pulperias.tagline: The corner shop on every block
pulperias.blurb: The neighborhood shops on Maps: Minisuper Alba (Av. El Albinal, Iglesia El Nazareno), El Pescador Miscelánea (Av. Central), Pick and Go, Miscelánea El Mercadito, Pulpería Ibarra (Av. El Tropezón), Pulpería Díaz, Pulpería Eduvijes. Rice, eggs, a cold bag of water — cash, a few doors from wherever you sleep.
pulperias.hours: Usually open from morning to night

saba.blurb: The chain, north of the park. Medicine, baby products, personal care and what they advertise as the lowest prices in town. Delivery through the national line. Opens early and closes late.
saba.tip: North side of the park. Orders ☎ 2298-2380.

cristo.blurb: The 25-meter Cristo on the south hill. White stone, the whole half-moon at your feet, boats in the bay. A short, steep climb from the south end of the beach: about 20 minutes, bring water. Go at opening or late afternoon; at midday it burns.

faro.tagline: The lighthouse of the two bays

ometepe.tagline: Day trip to the two volcanoes

vista-alegre.blurb: The signature villa inside La Santa María: 9 bedrooms, 9.5 baths, 10 beds, sleeps 20. About 8,000 square feet, inside and out, with ocean and bay views from every wing. Private pool, A/C in every suite, daily cleaning, butler, 24-hour security and concierge. Chef and grocery stocking on request. Five minutes down the hill to town.

eden-chocolata.blurb: Wellness retreat center in La Chocolata: yoga, surf, nature and plant-based food. Pool, shuttle to town and eight-day retreats from US$649.

flamingo.blurb: Adults-only boutique stay across from Playa Remanso, 10 minutes south of town. King suites with ocean views or the whole house, a cedar sauna facing the beach, private chef and breakfast included.

hotel-marea.blurb: Container building 100 m from Playa Remanso, with 13 rooms including doubles, twins and a four-bed dorm. Shared kitchen, terrace, garden and parking; strong fans, no A/C.

barrio-cafe.tagline: Hotel and café, a block from the sea
barrio-cafe.blurb: Six-room hotel downtown, a block from the bay, with its own restaurant and café, Barrio Café. Terrace with hammocks over the town's rooftops.

hermosa-ecolodge.blurb: Nica-owned ecolodge 12 km south, steps from Playa Hermosa, where Survivor was filmed. The main house is built entirely of genízaro wood; ocean-view rooms from US$45 and dorm beds from US$20, with breakfast and solar power.

todo-bien.blurb: Boutique eco lodge on the hill behind Playa Maderas, a short walk from the waves. Rustic luxury cabins, a pool with hammocks and a yoga platform in the trees overlooking the Pacific.

villas-mexico.blurb: Hostel 100 meters from Playa Marsella, with dorms from US$25, rooms and bungalows. Pool with day pass, Nica and Mexican cooking, surf lessons and kayaks.

elementos-del-sur.blurb: Large house in La Talanguera, steps from the beach and about an eight-minute walk from town: six bedrooms for up to 16 people, pool, A/C and fiber internet. Rented whole through Mango Vacation Rentals from US$390 a night.

nalu-nalu.blurb: Small hostel on the main street downtown, near shuttles, restaurants and the bay. Common area with hammocks and a shared kitchen; no physical front desk and cash payment.

bliss-resort.blurb: New resort, opened in September 2026 inside the Cala Azul community, between the forest and the sea, about 10 minutes from town. Bungalows and rooms with Pacific views, terrace and A/C, yoga and the Cala Azul restaurant, open to the public. Opening rates of US$150 to US$220 with breakfast.
bliss-resort.area: Cala Azul · Road to La Chocolata

g-plaza-colon.blurb: The mansion on Parque Central. Rooms face the cathedral, with a courtyard pool and the rocking-chair corridor that is Granada. You step out and you're on the plaza.
g-plaza-colon.tip: Ask for a room facing the plaza: at sunset the sun hits the yellow facade.

g-gran-francia.blurb: Corner mansion a block from the park: thick walls, a pool and the restaurant in the courtyard. Old-money Granada, still the luxury address.

g-malinche.blurb: Quiet rooms around two courtyards and a pool, a block from La Calzada: you hear the street, but you don't sleep on it.

g-casa-sf.blurb: Next to the old San Francisco convent: rooms, a restaurant Granadans still book and the yellow-and-blue block. Breakfast in the courtyard.

g-corazon.blurb: Boutique hotel with 15 rooms on Calle Santa Lucía, with a pool, hammocks and a famous breakfast. It's a social enterprise: 100% of profits go to education projects.

g-socialtel.blurb: Dorms and private rooms, coworking and a pool: the house for backpackers and digital nomads. It used to be Selina and is still the meeting point if you want a desk and a drink.

g-boca.blurb: The hostel people name first. Hammocks, a kitchen and rooms that fill up by afternoon; the park is a short walk away.

g-azul.blurb: Cheap bed, breakfast included and loaner bikes. The simple hostel that keeps working when the expensive places are full.

g-colonial.tagline: The former Hotel Colonial, now IHG
g-colonial.blurb: The former Hotel Colonial, renovated and reopened in May 2025 as an IHG voco hotel, 50 meters from the cathedral and Parque Central. 36 rooms (10 suites), two pools and a spa.

g-miss-marigran.blurb: Colonial house turned six-room B&B, a block and a half north of Iglesia Xalteva. Two garden courtyards, a pool, parking and homemade breakfast included; from about US$70.

g-casa-consulado.blurb: Restored early-19th-century colonial house, a block from Parque Central: four rooms with A/C, a full kitchen, a courtyard with a pool and a rooftop with views of volcanoes and bell towers. Rented whole for up to 8 people (US$280 a night, three-night minimum).

g-garden.blurb: The courtyard everyone names. Fountain, hammock, salads and coffee, shop in the back. A block from the park. Full at noon.

g-dario.blurb: Colonial rooms and a pool in the mansion named for the poet, a block from the park. Quieter than La Calzada after ten.

g-alhambra.blurb: On Parque Central: rocking chairs in the corridor and rooms facing the cathedral. A hotel from the Granada of old.

g-oasis.tagline: Hostel with a pool and tours
g-oasis.blurb: Classic downtown hostel, a few blocks from Parque Central, with a pool, hammocks and free breakfast. They run tours to Laguna de Apoyo and Masaya volcano; quiet hours from 11 pm.

g-jicaro.blurb: Luxury eco lodge on a private island in Las Isletas, reached by boat from Granada. Nine two-story casitas facing the lake, a pool, spa and full board; from about US$990 a night per casita.

g-paradiso.blurb: Hostel on the shore of Laguna de Apoyo, about 11 km from Granada, with a private beach and a restaurant over the water. Dorms, family rooms and a day pass for those who only come to swim.

g-tribal.blurb: Boutique design hotel on a quiet downtown street: seven rooms (five Premium and two Junior Suites) around a garden with a pool. Featured in Condé Nast Traveler and Travel + Leisure.

g-pacaya.blurb: Boutique lodge on the rim of the Laguna de Apoyo crater, on the Catarina side. 26 rooms with lagoon views, a spa and a restaurant; from about US$125 a night.

g-treehouse.blurb: Hostel in the treetops, in the jungle about 10 km from Granada, with hanging bridges between the little houses. Open Thursday through Sunday with a three-night minimum; shuttle from Granada on Thursday at noon and a party on Friday from 4 pm to 3 am.

g-white-rabbit.blurb: Small, colorful hostel on Calle La Libertad, with murals, a pool and an open-air kitchen. Near-perfect rating on Hostelworld; there's a bar next door, so bring earplugs.

g-san-simian.tagline: Bungalows on the shore of Apoyo
g-san-simian.blurb: Six bungalows on the shore of Laguna de Apoyo, with a restaurant and direct water access for swimming. Pickup from Granada available.

g-jardin.blurb: Family-run ten-room hotel on Calle La Otra Banda, five blocks from Parque Central. Garden with coffee, cacao and citrus, a pool with a bar, buffet breakfast and parking; from about US$65.

g-secret-garden.blurb: Boutique hotel on Calle Santa Lucía, with rooms around a pool courtyard and a lush plant garden. Very well rated (9.2 on Booking); from about US$80.

g-los-patios.blurb: Five-room design hotel on Calle Corrales: a colonial mansion with modern lines, courtyards, a pool and breakfast included. From about US$95 plus tax.

g-coco-bay.blurb: Hostel on the shore of Laguna de Apoyo with direct water access, free kayaks and a communal dinner every night. Dorms from about US$20.

g-gallo-pinto.blurb: Small hostel downtown, with colorful rooms, a shared kitchen and a garden. Rated 9.3 on Hostelworld.

g-hotel-consulado.blurb: Restored 19th-century mansion on Calle El Consulado, two blocks from the cathedral: 13 rooms with A/C, a pool and Nica or international breakfast included. Not the same as Casa Consulado, the rental house on the same street.

g-villa-adela.blurb: Colonial mansion with four suites, two courtyards and a private pool, a block and a half from Iglesia San Francisco toward the lake. Rented by the suite or whole for up to 12 people (from about US$525 a night).

g-estacion.tagline: The train that no longer runs

l-convento.blurb: Convent hotel a block from the cathedral. Cloister, art and a pool in the old garden. León's quiet address.

l-los-balcones.blurb: Colonial rooms with a balcony over the street. You walk the grid and come back to the courtyard.

l-bigfoot.blurb: The backpacker house that books Cerro Negro. Dorms, a bar and sometimes a bus to the beach. The sandboard tour is booked at reception.

l-jardin.blurb: Hostel with a garden. Quieter than Bigfoot and just as central. Hammocks when the heat eases.

l-via-via.blurb: Rooms upstairs and a courtyard bar that closes late. Sometimes there's live music. You eat here even if you sleep somewhere else.

l-lazybones.blurb: A pool in the middle of the house. Dorms and private rooms. The other Bigfoot when that one is full.

l-tortuga.blurb: Hostel house a few blocks from the park. Kitchen, porch and a slower León.

l-sesteo.blurb: Tables in the park. Toña, sometimes a band, León's postcard lunch. Tourist prices; the view is the cathedral.

l-cocinarte.blurb: Vegetarian dishes in a colonial room. The break from gallo pinto and carne asada.

l-manana.blurb: Coffee, eggs and a slow morning after Cerro Negro. One of the new places people name.

l-tacos.blurb: The taco stand students know. Cheap, open late and no park surcharge.

l-chinitos.blurb: The Chinese-Nica counter. Rice, chop suey and a cold fresco. Local lunch.

l-coco.blurb: Juices, fruit and a light plate when the heat wins. Good after climbing the rooftop.

l-tabaco.blurb: Cocktails and kitchen until late. The place to dress up when you miss the rhythm of the Calzada.

l-playas-destacado.blurb: Twenty minutes west. Dark sand, boats and city folks on Sunday. Las Peñitas is the hostel beach; Poneloya is the family one.
l-playas-destacado.tip: Bus or taxi from the market. Swim carefully: the waves hit hard.

l-poneloya.blurb: León's old beach town. Restaurants on the sand, families on Sunday and a wave that breaks hard. Sunset on the rocks.

l-penitas.blurb: The backpacker beach. Surf lessons, seafood and the mangrove next door. Sleep here if the city heat is already enough.

l-isla-juan.blurb: The reserve south of Peñitas. Kayaking in the mangrove and turtles in season. A morning trip from the beach hotels.

l-via-night.blurb: The courtyard that fills up after nine. Students, travelers and a band when there is one. Start here.

l-sesteo-night.blurb: A drink in front of the white facade. Early, before the hostels turn up the volume.

l-mirador.blurb: A rooftop, when it's open. The grid and the cathedral from above.

l-bigfoot-night.blurb: The hostel bar. Cheap rum and the pre-party before the beach bus. Earplugs if you sleep upstairs.

l-catedral.blurb: Heritage site. Climb to the roof: white lime, volcanoes and the bells. Rubén Darío is inside. The ticket is for the terrace.
l-catedral.tip: Go early. The photo is the roof.

l-parque.blurb: The cathedral plaza. Lions, vendors and a bench in the shade. This is where you get your bearings.

l-cerro.blurb: The young black cone. You climb with a board and come down over the ash. Half a day from any hostel. Clothes you can throw away.
l-cerro.tip: The afternoon light is better. Bring a bandana for the dust.

l-telica.blurb: Active crater and sunset. Longer than Cerro Negro. Book with someone who brings water and a flashlight.

l-recoleccion.blurb: The yellow baroque church. Carved facade, a short stop between parks.

l-ortiz.blurb: Fundación Ortíz Gurdián. Two mansions and a real collection: painting and sculpture. The indoor break when León burns.

l-subtiava.blurb: The indigenous parish west of the grid. San Juan Bautista. Another León, different from the park.

l-bigfoot-tours.blurb: The hostel's desk. Sandboarding, Telica and the shuttle to Peñitas. The usual booking.

l-va-pues-leon.blurb: Independent counters near the park. Compare the Cerro Negro price with Bigfoot before paying.

l-bici.blurb: Bikes at the hostels. The colonial grid is best seen by bike. Lock it up in the park.

l-bus-playa.tagline: From the market to the sea
l-bus-playa.blurb: Bus from the market to Poneloya and Peñitas. Cheap, slow and local. Take a taxi if you carry boards.

l-pali.blurb: To stock the house. Water, chicken, beer. Fruit is still better at the market.

l-colonia.blurb: The bigger supermarket. Imports when Palí doesn't have them.

l-mercado.blurb: The city market. Beach buses leave from here. Fruit, meat and plastic chairs.

l-saba.blurb: The national chain in León. After the volcano, for sun and dust relief.

l-farm-central.blurb: Independent counter near the cathedral. Cash and generics.

l-perla.blurb: Big mansion, a pool and homey rooms. A few blocks from the cathedral.

l-austria.blurb: Small hotel, decent rooms and breakfast. The middle ground when El Convento is full.

l-surfing-turtle.blurb: Eco lodge on the sand on Isla Los Brasiles, reached by a short boat ride from Poneloya. Cabins and dorms, surf and turtles in season. Sleep on the beach, not in the heat of downtown.

l-puesta-sol.blurb: Cabins and Italian cooking on the beach. You watch the sunset from your table.

l-casa-adobe.blurb: Remodeled colonial house rented whole for up to 7 people: three bedrooms, a pool with hammocks and an equipped kitchen, in a good neighborhood. Rated 4.86 on Airbnb.

l-poco-a-poco.blurb: Award-winning downtown hostel (it bills itself as the best in Nicaragua three years running), with a pool and a rooftop terrace. It has a second location, Poco a Poco Junior, and its own tour agency, Hola Hola Tours.

l-marriott.blurb: Chain hotel next to La Recolección church, a few blocks from the cathedral. 50 rooms with A/C, a gym, a restaurant with a bar and parking; from about US$80.

l-mano-a-mano.blurb: Beachfront hostel in Las Peñitas, next to the Isla Juan Venado reserve, with a beach bar and restaurant, surf lessons and daily yoga. Beds from about US$13.

l-flor-de-sarta.blurb: Boutique hotel two blocks west of Parque San Juan, with a pool, a patio with plants, breakfast and parking. From about US$55.

l-the-spot.blurb: Social, adults-only hostel downtown, with free breakfast and A/C at night. Designed for meeting people without losing sleep.

l-hotel-azul.blurb: Ten-room boutique hotel two and a half blocks north of the cathedral, with a courtyard pool and a restaurant serving healthy and international food. From about US$85.

l-tranquilo.blurb: Small boutique hotel on the waterfront in Las Peñitas: four rooms, a pool, a rancho and hammocks. From about US$80.

l-barca-de-oro.blurb: Hotel and restaurant in Las Peñitas, facing the Isla Juan Venado reserve and steps from the beach. From dorms to family bungalows, with a spa, free bikes and breakfast; from about US$30.

l-al-sole.blurb: Guesthouse in a downtown mansion, two blocks west of Iglesia Zaragoza, with a pool and a garden. Rooms from US$24 to US$52, most with breakfast.

l-el-simple.blurb: Rustic lodge with seven suites right on the sand in Las Peñitas, facing a good wave and with a covered pool that opens onto the beach. Each suite is booked on Airbnb (one is a treehouse for ten) or you can rent the whole lodge.

l-casa-lula.blurb: Small hostel in barrio El Sagrario, near the cathedral, with dorms and private rooms from US$13 to US$28.

l-el-albergue.blurb: A hostel of the classic kind in a Nica house downtown, with a patio and hammocks. Rated 8.5 on Hostelworld.

l-suyapa.blurb: Beachfront hotel between Las Peñitas and Poneloya, with a pool, a seafood and grill restaurant, and a wave to surf out front. Rooms for one to five people; from about US$60.

l-pan-paz.blurb: Bread, quiche and coffee. The French counter León names for breakfast.

l-jardin-secreto.blurb: A hidden garden, a plate and a drink. Dinner away from the park.

l-mediterraneo.blurb: Hummus, pita and salad when the heat won't let you eat meat. Downtown.

l-pure-earth.blurb: Smoothies and bowls. The healthy room after Cerro Negro.

l-sua.blurb: Grill on the beach. Fish, cold beer and the Sunday table after a swim.

l-mono-loco.blurb: Beach bar in Peñitas. Tacos, a cocktail and sand on the floor.

l-olla.blurb: A León bar students still use. Cheaper than the terraces on the park.

l-don-senor.blurb: When Via Via closes the kitchen, the night continues here. Check the door: in León the night moves around.

l-revolucion.blurb: On the park. Guides who fought in the war and a rooftop over the cathedral. One hour, a tip and 1979.
l-revolucion.tip: Tip the guide. The view is the roof.

l-calvario.tagline: At the end of the street
l-calvario.blurb: The colorful church at the end of the east axis. A photo and a short stop on the walk.

l-leon-viejo.blurb: The first León, buried and unburied by the lake, under Momotombo. Half a day. Ruins, not the living city.

l-flor-cana.blurb: The rum house in Chichigalpa, a trip from León. Distillery tour and tasting. The shuttle is booked downtown.

l-quetzal.blurb: Nonprofit guides. Telica, Cerro Negro and multi-day routes. The money goes to projects with children. Book a day ahead.

l-maxipali.blurb: Cart and cases of water. The weekly shop for a house.

l-farm-subtiava.blurb: Counter in the old neighborhood. Generics, cash and faster than the park.

l-salinas-grandes.blurb: Fishing village south of Juan Venado. A long, nearly empty beach, boats on the sand and the salt flats that give it its name. Surfable waves when the swell is in.
l-salinas-grandes.tip: About 45 minutes by car or taxi from León. There are buses, but few; bring water and cash.

l-puerto-sandino.blurb: Nagarote's fishing port, with a wide dark-sand beach next to it, Playa Azul. Surf waves, long sunsets and simple seafood in town.
l-puerto-sandino.tip: About an hour by car from León on the highway to Managua and the Puerto Sandino turnoff.

l-el-transito.blurb: Fishing village on the Managua coast, past Puerto Sandino. Dark sand, volcanic rock formations and calm pools at low tide. Fresh seafood at the beach ranchos.
l-el-transito.tip: About 1 h 15 min by car from León on the new highway to Managua and the El Tránsito turnoff. The pools are best at low tide.

l-jiquilillo.blurb: Fishing village in Chinandega, north of León. Miles of dark sand under the palms, surfable waves and quiet beach hostels. The Padre Ramos estuary is right next door.
l-jiquilillo.tip: About 2 hours by car from León via Chinandega and El Viejo. There are also buses from El Viejo. Bring cash: ATMs are scarce.

l-padre-ramos.blurb: Nature reserve next to Jiquilillo. An estuary beach with calm water, mangroves to explore by boat or kayak and turtles nesting in season. Packed with families at Easter.
l-padre-ramos.tip: About 2 h 15 min by car from León via Chinandega, El Viejo and the Jiquilillo road. Boat tours leave from Padre Ramos village.

delivery-san-juan.blurb: Home delivery from San Juan del Sur restaurants such as Dockside, Pompeya Pizza, Maggy’s Steak House, Dale Pues (Tropical Garden Café & Dining) and Vicky’s Pizza. Order on WhatsApp and they bring it to you.
delivery-san-juan.tip: WhatsApp +505 8411 3602. The catalog with restaurants and menus is on their WhatsApp profile.

fuente-chocolate.blurb: Chocolate shop and café. A variety of organic Nicaraguan chocolates and coffees, natural smoothies and other hot and cold drinks, a variety of delicious desserts, whole or sliced cakes, healthy vegan products, artisan baguette sandwiches and more...
fuente-chocolate.tip: Try the hot chocolate or the brownie with ice cream. Vegan desserts are marked in the display case. WhatsApp +505 8764 0989.

casa-la-nina.blurb: House for short or long-term rent, modern style, spacious, 3 bedrooms for 8 people, a 5-minute walk from downtown and the beach, beautiful views over the sea, the town and the countryside, 2 covered terraces, A/C, jacuzzi...

gym-move-viva.blurb: A modern, clean gym open 7 days a week on Paseo del Rey, where Crazy Crab used to be (20 m north of Hotel Anamar). Machines, Olympic bars, spin bikes, group classes and personal training.
gym-move-viva.tip: Day pass US$5, week US$20, month US$30 (paying in person). WhatsApp +505 8553 3296.

gym-fight-club.blurb: The biggest gym in town, 1.5 blocks east of the market. Free weights, machines, a boxing ring and mats, with boxing, CrossFit, MMA and jiu-jitsu classes.
gym-fight-club.tip: ☎ 2568-2192. Private boxing lessons with Carlos. Instagram @fightclubgym_sjds.

gym-gymsito.tagline: Weights at the end of the beach
gym-gymsito.blurb: A small, well-equipped gym at the north end of the beach, on Paseo del Rey. Plenty of machines and free weights at a good price. No air conditioning; closed at midday and on Sundays.
gym-gymsito.tip: Day pass about C$180. Bring a towel: it is required to get in.

gym-moju-fight.tagline: MMA, Muay Thai, BJJ and boxing
gym-moju-fight.blurb: A martial arts gym since 2008, upstairs above Dockside at the port. Group and private BJJ, MMA, Muay Thai and boxing classes for all levels, with gloves, heavy bags and a weight rack.
gym-moju-fight.tip: Class US$6, day US$10, month US$40, no contract. Pay downstairs at Dockside. WhatsApp +505 8485 3176.

apartamentos-la-playa.tagline: 200 m from the beach, right downtown
apartamentos-la-playa.blurb: Just 200 meters from the beach, right in the center of San Juan del Sur. A fully equipped apartment: queen bed plus sofa bed, full kitchen with microwave, fridge and coffee maker, and WiFi included. Food and drinks are allowed. Comfortable, private and safe; ideal for couples.
apartamentos-la-playa.area: Downtown · south side of the church
apartamentos-la-playa.tip: Next to the old library, on the south side of the church. WhatsApp +505 8816 7161 (Yanaisy Ércia).

text.Villa de cinco recámaras en La Santa Mar: Five-bedroom villa in La Santa María, facing west over the bay of San Juan del Sur. Sleeps ten, 4.5 baths, private pool, A/C in every room, generator and cistern. The terrace is the point: the sailfish on the wall, the glass railing and the Pacific turning to gold.
text.El pueblo queda a cinco minutos, bajando: The town is five minutes away, down the hill. Villa guests can use the resort's pool, gym, clubhouse and coworking.
text.Hotel y residencias en la loma sobre San: Hotel and residences on the hill above San Juan del Sur. Infinity pool facing the bay, gym and yoga, fiber-internet coworking, clubhouse, snack bar, courts and a pirate-ship playground. Gatehouse, 24/7 concierge, five minutes from town.
text.Toca cada amenidad. Sunset Home Villa #2: Tap each amenity. Sunset Home Villa #2 is the five-bedroom villa on the hill.
text.Media cuadra del parque: Half a block from the park
text.Naranja, una cuadra del mercado: Orange building, a block from the market
text.Al sur del cementerio municipal, a 1.2 k: South of the municipal cemetery, 1.2 km from the center. A pool with a real waterfall, garden, grill, terrace, rooms with A/C or fan. Parking and 24-hour security. The quiet getaway when you want water without a resort price.
text.Frecostado sur del cementerio municipal: South side of the San Pablo municipal cemetery. Beach about a 15-minute walk. Cash payment on arrival. No breakfast.
text.Piscina a dos cuadras de la playa: Pool two blocks from the beach
text.Hotel en La Talanguera, a dos cuadras de: Hotel in La Talanguera, two blocks from the beach and a ten-minute walk along the sand to the center. Fruit-tree garden, big pool and a free shuttle from Casa Oro Eco Hostel; rooms from US$35.
text.Hotel boutique familiar de 18 cuartos en: Family-run boutique hotel with 18 rooms in the heart of the port, steps from the sea, founded by doña Guadalupe Morales. Its restaurant El Buen Gusto, serving Nica food and seafood, sits right on the main beach.
text.Hotel en una colina unos 500 m al este d: Hotel on a hill about 500 m east of Playa Maderas, with ocean-view rooms, a pool with a bar and yoga. The walk down to the beach is short but steep.
text.Surf camp ecológico en el bosque cerca d: Eco surf camp in the forest near Marsella: a three-story bamboo main building with a restaurant, bar and yoga on top, and ten raised cabins across dorms, twins and suites. Pool with a bar, surf lessons and yoga.
text.Surf hostel con skate bowl: Surf hostel with a skate bowl
text.Surf hostel a pocos minutos a pie de Pla: Surf hostel a few minutes' walk from Playa Maderas, with jungle cabins, its own concrete skate bowl and a yoga deck. Dorms from US$15 and private rooms from US$40.
text.El antiguo Selina Maderas, 200 m al nort: The former Selina Maderas, 200 m north of the Marsella junction and a few minutes' walk from the beach. Dorms, tipis and suites around the pool, with a restaurant, yoga deck and coworking.
text.Hotel boutique y retiro sobre Playa Esca: Boutique hotel and retreat on Playa Escameca, south of town: five little houses with ocean views and two rooms by the pool. Surf school, open-air yoga studio and transfers from Managua or Liberia.
text.Hotel boutique y centro de retiros a cin: Boutique hotel and retreat center five minutes from Playa Marsella, next to Maderas. Rooms with A/C and hot water, a pool, a restaurant and a yoga space with an ocean view.
text.Hostal eco con piscina infinity: Eco hostel with an infinity pool
text.Hostal solo para adultos en una loma a u: Adults-only hostel on a hill about 3 km from town, with a pool, hammocks and the sunset over the bay. Breakfast included, shared kitchen and a free shuttle to town; no air conditioning.
text.Doce unidades en siete acres de jardín,: Twelve units on seven acres of garden, four minutes by car from Playa Marsella and eight from Maderas. One-bedroom bungalows and two-bedroom ranchers with a kitchen and A/C, a pool and a restaurant.
text.Eco lodge con piscina infinity: Eco lodge with an infinity pool
text.Eco lodge a cinco minutos a pie de Playa: Eco lodge a five-minute walk from Playa Maderas, almost entirely solar-powered. Infinity pool with a 180° ocean view, yoga studio, rooftop for the sunset and breakfast included.
text.Eco lodge de seis cabañas de madera en l: Eco lodge of six wooden cabins in the jungle above Playa Maderas, with an infinity deck among the trees for yoga and sunsets. Surf packages and dinners by Nica chefs; no A/C, just fans.
text.El mostrador y la mesa de mariscos. Sopa: The seafood counter and table. Soup, fish in cream sauce with shrimp, tostones. The home of Esterlina Sevilla Alvarado: first the fish market, then the plate.
text.Pizza en el food park del puerto: Pizza at the port food park
text.Carrito frente a Tio Milton: Food cart across from Tio Milton
text.Tacos con vista al puerto: Tacos with a view of the port
text.Pizza sanjuaneña a domicilio, delivery g: San Juan-style pizza delivered to your door, free delivery. Thick, oven-baked crust: ham, pepperoni, chicken, creole chorizo, Hawaiian, vegetarian, jalapeño, mushroom or mixed. Red sauce or pesto, and a cheese crust if you like. Personal C$240, medium C$330, family C$370, extra-family C$470. With cheese crust, C$300 to C$600.
text.Buffet local, 50 m del UNO: Local buffet, 50 m from the UNO
text.De Rest. El Timón, 200 m al norte, frent: From Rest. El Timón, 200 m north, on the beachfront. Instagram @sunnybeachbar.
text.Comedor de pared verde en San Juan del S: Green-walled comedor in San Juan del Sur. The name is hand-painted: El Rincón de María, Sazón Leones. The sidewalk chalkboard announces lunch for C$100, fresco included. Rice, beans, plantain slices and the stew of the day.
text.El precio está en el pizarrón. Pregunta: The price is on the chalkboard. Ask about the fresco of the day.
text.Alberca, alitas, 1 c. del UNO: Pool, wings, 1 block from the UNO
text.WhatsApp +505 8159-6777. Costado norte d: WhatsApp +505 8159-6777. North side of the roundabout.
text.La media luna por la que viniste. Lancha: The half-moon you came for. Boats on the sand, the malecón, the Cristo on the south hill and a sunset that stops traffic. Don't swim in the morning; walk the beach as the sun goes down. This is the town beach. Everything else is a taxi ride.
text.El final de la costanera: The end of the coastal road
text.La palapa del puerto cuando hay banda: m: The port's palapa when there's a band: live music Friday through Sunday, a full bar and the bay a few steps away. Seafood if you're still hungry. The local night out, no cover.
text.Día o semana: By the day or the week
text.El súper Walmart del puente, barrio Las: The Walmart supermarket by the bridge, in barrio Las Pampas. Rice, beans, chicken, vegetables, beer, cleaning supplies: the cheapest full shop in town. Full aisles, cards accepted. Stock up here and buy fruit at Guevara.
text.La esquina de cada cuadra: The corner shop on every block
text.Suelen abrir de mañana a noche: Usually open from morning to night
text.La cadena, al norte del parque. Medicina: The chain, north of the park. Medicine, baby products, personal care and what they advertise as the lowest prices in town. Delivery through the national line. Opens early and closes late.
text.Costado norte del parque. Pedidos ☎ 2298: North side of the park. Orders ☎ 2298-2380.
The 25-meter Cristo on the south hill. White stone, the whole half-moon at your feet, boats in the bay. A short, steep climb from the south end of the beach: about 20 minutes, bring water. Go at opening or late afternoon; at midday it burns.
text.El faro de las dos bahías: The lighthouse of the two bays
text.Día a los dos volcanes: Day trip to the two volcanoes
text.La villa firma dentro de La Santa María:: The signature villa inside La Santa María: 9 bedrooms, 9.5 baths, 10 beds, sleeps 20. About 8,000 square feet, inside and out, with ocean and bay views from every wing. Private pool, A/C in every suite, daily cleaning, butler, 24-hour security and concierge. Chef and grocery stocking on request. Five minutes down the hill to town.
text.Centro de retiros de bienestar en La Cho: Wellness retreat center in La Chocolata: yoga, surf, nature and plant-based food. Pool, shuttle to town and eight-day retreats from US$649.
text.Estancia boutique solo para adultos fren: Adults-only boutique stay across from Playa Remanso, 10 minutes south of town. King suites with ocean views or the whole house, a cedar sauna facing the beach, private chef and breakfast included.
text.Edificio de contenedores a 100 m de Play: Container building 100 m from Playa Remanso, with 13 rooms including doubles, twins and a four-bed dorm. Shared kitchen, terrace, garden and parking; strong fans, no A/C.
text.Hotel y café, una cuadra del mar: Hotel and café, a block from the sea
text.Hotel de seis cuartos en el centro, a un: Six-room hotel downtown, a block from the bay, with its own restaurant and café, Barrio Café. Terrace with hammocks over the town's rooftops.
text.Ecolodge de dueños nicas a 12 km al sur,: Nica-owned ecolodge 12 km south, steps from Playa Hermosa, where Survivor was filmed. The main house is built entirely of genízaro wood; ocean-view rooms from US$45 and dorm beds from US$20, with breakfast and solar power.
text.Eco lodge boutique en la loma detrás de: Boutique eco lodge on the hill behind Playa Maderas, a short walk from the waves. Rustic luxury cabins, a pool with hammocks and a yoga platform in the trees overlooking the Pacific.
text.Hostal a 100 metros de Playa Marsella, c: Hostel 100 meters from Playa Marsella, with dorms from US$25, rooms and bungalows. Pool with day pass, Nica and Mexican cooking, surf lessons and kayaks.
text.Casa grande en La Talanguera, a pasos de: Large house in La Talanguera, steps from the beach and about an eight-minute walk from town: six bedrooms for up to 16 people, pool, A/C and fiber internet. Rented whole through Mango Vacation Rentals from US$390 a night.
text.Hostal pequeño en la calle principal del: Small hostel on the main street downtown, near shuttles, restaurants and the bay. Common area with hammocks and a shared kitchen; no physical front desk and cash payment.
text.Resort nuevo, abierto en septiembre de 2: New resort, opened in September 2026 inside the Cala Azul community, between the forest and the sea, about 10 minutes from town. Bungalows and rooms with Pacific views, terrace and A/C, yoga and the Cala Azul restaurant, open to the public. Opening rates of US$150 to US$220 with breakfast.
text.Cala Azul · Camino a La Chocolata: Cala Azul · Road to La Chocolata
text.La casona del Parque Central. Los cuarto: The mansion on Parque Central. Rooms face the cathedral, with a courtyard pool and the rocking-chair corridor that is Granada. You step out and you're on the plaza.
text.Pide un cuarto hacia la plaza: al atarde: Ask for a room facing the plaza: at sunset the sun hits the yellow facade.
text.Casona de esquina a una cuadra del parqu: Corner mansion a block from the park: thick walls, a pool and the restaurant in the courtyard. Old-money Granada, still the luxury address.
text.Cuartos tranquilos alrededor de dos pati: Quiet rooms around two courtyards and a pool, a block from La Calzada: you hear the street, but you don't sleep on it.
text.Junto al antiguo convento San Francisco:: Next to the old San Francisco convent: rooms, a restaurant Granadans still book and the yellow-and-blue block. Breakfast in the courtyard.
text.Hotel boutique de 15 cuartos en la Calle: Boutique hotel with 15 rooms on Calle Santa Lucía, with a pool, hammocks and a famous breakfast. It's a social enterprise: 100% of profits go to education projects.
text.Dorms y privados, coworking y piscina: l: Dorms and private rooms, coworking and a pool: the house for backpackers and digital nomads. It used to be Selina and is still the meeting point if you want a desk and a drink.
text.El hostal que la gente nombra primero. H: The hostel people name first. Hammocks, a kitchen and rooms that fill up by afternoon; the park is a short walk away.
text.Cama barata, desayuno incluido y bicis p: Cheap bed, breakfast included and loaner bikes. The simple hostel that keeps working when the expensive places are full.
text.El ex Hotel Colonial, ahora IHG: The former Hotel Colonial, now IHG
text.El antiguo Hotel Colonial, renovado y re: The former Hotel Colonial, renovated and reopened in May 2025 as an IHG voco hotel, 50 meters from the cathedral and Parque Central. 36 rooms (10 suites), two pools and a spa.
text.Casa colonial convertida en B&B de seis: Colonial house turned six-room B&B, a block and a half north of Iglesia Xalteva. Two garden courtyards, a pool, parking and homemade breakfast included; from about US$70.
text.Casa colonial de principios del siglo XI: Restored early-19th-century colonial house, a block from Parque Central: four rooms with A/C, a full kitchen, a courtyard with a pool and a rooftop with views of volcanoes and bell towers. Rented whole for up to 8 people (US$280 a night, three-night minimum).
text.El patio que todo el mundo nombra. Fuent: The courtyard everyone names. Fountain, hammock, salads and coffee, shop in the back. A block from the park. Full at noon.
text.Cuartos coloniales y piscina en la cason: Colonial rooms and a pool in the mansion named for the poet, a block from the park. Quieter than La Calzada after ten.
text.Sobre el Parque Central: mecedoras en el: On Parque Central: rocking chairs in the corridor and rooms facing the cathedral. A hotel from the Granada of old.
text.Hostal con piscina y tours: Hostel with a pool and tours
text.Hostal clásico del centro, a pocas cuadr: Classic downtown hostel, a few blocks from Parque Central, with a pool, hammocks and free breakfast. They run tours to Laguna de Apoyo and Masaya volcano; quiet hours from 11 pm.
text.Eco lodge de lujo en una isla privada de: Luxury eco lodge on a private island in Las Isletas, reached by boat from Granada. Nine two-story casitas facing the lake, a pool, spa and full board; from about US$990 a night per casita.
text.Hostal a la orilla de la Laguna de Apoyo: Hostel on the shore of Laguna de Apoyo, about 11 km from Granada, with a private beach and a restaurant over the water. Dorms, family rooms and a day pass for those who only come to swim.
text.Hotel boutique de diseño en una calle tr: Boutique design hotel on a quiet downtown street: seven rooms (five Premium and two Junior Suites) around a garden with a pool. Featured in Condé Nast Traveler and Travel + Leisure.
text.Lodge boutique en el borde del cráter de: Boutique lodge on the rim of the Laguna de Apoyo crater, on the Catarina side. 26 rooms with lagoon views, a spa and a restaurant; from about US$125 a night.
text.Hostal en las copas de los árboles, en l: Hostel in the treetops, in the jungle about 10 km from Granada, with hanging bridges between the little houses. Open Thursday through Sunday with a three-night minimum; shuttle from Granada on Thursday at noon and a party on Friday from 4 pm to 3 am.
text.Hostal pequeño y colorido en la Calle La: Small, colorful hostel on Calle La Libertad, with murals, a pool and an open-air kitchen. Near-perfect rating on Hostelworld; there's a bar next door, so bring earplugs.
text.Bungalows a la orilla de Apoyo: Bungalows on the shore of Apoyo
text.Seis bungalows a la orilla de la Laguna: Six bungalows on the shore of Laguna de Apoyo, with a restaurant and direct water access for swimming. Pickup from Granada available.
text.Hotel familiar de diez cuartos en la cal: Family-run ten-room hotel on Calle La Otra Banda, five blocks from Parque Central. Garden with coffee, cacao and citrus, a pool with a bar, buffet breakfast and parking; from about US$65.
text.Hotel boutique en la Calle Santa Lucía,: Boutique hotel on Calle Santa Lucía, with rooms around a pool courtyard and a lush plant garden. Very well rated (9.2 on Booking); from about US$80.
text.Hotel de diseño de cinco cuartos en la C: Five-room design hotel on Calle Corrales: a colonial mansion with modern lines, courtyards, a pool and breakfast included. From about US$95 plus tax.
text.Hostal a la orilla de la Laguna de Apoyo: Hostel on the shore of Laguna de Apoyo with direct water access, free kayaks and a communal dinner every night. Dorms from about US$20.
text.Hostal pequeño en el centro, con cuartos: Small hostel downtown, with colorful rooms, a shared kitchen and a garden. Rated 9.3 on Hostelworld.
text.Casona del siglo XIX restaurada en la Ca: Restored 19th-century mansion on Calle El Consulado, two blocks from the cathedral: 13 rooms with A/C, a pool and Nica or international breakfast included. Not the same as Casa Consulado, the rental house on the same street.
text.Casona colonial de cuatro suites con dos: Colonial mansion with four suites, two courtyards and a private pool, a block and a half from Iglesia San Francisco toward the lake. Rented by the suite or whole for up to 12 people (from about US$525 a night).
text.El tren que ya no corre: The train that no longer runs
text.Hotel de convento a una cuadra de la cat: Convent hotel a block from the cathedral. Cloister, art and a pool in the old garden. León's quiet address.
text.Cuartos coloniales con balcón a la calle: Colonial rooms with a balcony over the street. You walk the grid and come back to the courtyard.
text.La casa de mochileros que reserva Cerro: The backpacker house that books Cerro Negro. Dorms, a bar and sometimes a bus to the beach. The sandboard tour is booked at reception.
text.Hostal con jardín. Más quieto que Bigfoo: Hostel with a garden. Quieter than Bigfoot and just as central. Hammocks when the heat eases.
text.Cuartos arriba y un bar de patio que cie: Rooms upstairs and a courtyard bar that closes late. Sometimes there's live music. You eat here even if you sleep somewhere else.
text.Piscina en el centro de la casa. Dormito: A pool in the middle of the house. Dorms and private rooms. The other Bigfoot when that one is full.
text.Casa-hostal a unas cuadras del parque. C: Hostel house a few blocks from the park. Kitchen, porch and a slower León.
text.Mesas en el parque. Toña, a veces banda,: Tables in the park. Toña, sometimes a band, León's postcard lunch. Tourist prices; the view is the cathedral.
text.Platos vegetarianos en un cuarto colonia: Vegetarian dishes in a colonial room. The break from gallo pinto and carne asada.
text.Café, huevos y una mañana lenta después: Coffee, eggs and a slow morning after Cerro Negro. One of the new places people name.
text.El puesto de tacos que conocen los estud: The taco stand students know. Cheap, open late and no park surcharge.
text.El mostrador chino-nica. Arroz, chop sue: The Chinese-Nica counter. Rice, chop suey and a cold fresco. Local lunch.
text.Jugos, fruta y un plato ligero cuando ga: Juices, fruit and a light plate when the heat wins. Good after climbing the rooftop.
text.Cócteles y cocina hasta tarde. El lugar: Cocktails and kitchen until late. The place to dress up when you miss the rhythm of the Calzada.
text.Veinte minutos al oeste. Arena oscura, l: Twenty minutes west. Dark sand, boats and city folks on Sunday. Las Peñitas is the hostel beach; Poneloya is the family one.
text.Bus o taxi desde el mercado. Nada con cu: Bus or taxi from the market. Swim carefully: the waves hit hard.
text.El pueblo de playa viejo de León. Restau: León's old beach town. Restaurants on the sand, families on Sunday and a wave that breaks hard. Sunset on the rocks.
text.La playa de mochileros. Clases de surf,: The backpacker beach. Surf lessons, seafood and the mangrove next door. Sleep here if the city heat is already enough.
text.La reserva al sur de Peñitas. Kayak en e: The reserve south of Peñitas. Kayaking in the mangrove and turtles in season. A morning trip from the beach hotels.
text.El patio que se llena después de las nue: The courtyard that fills up after nine. Students, travelers and a band when there is one. Start here.
text.Un trago frente a la fachada blanca. Tem: A drink in front of the white facade. Early, before the hostels turn up the volume.
text.Una azotea, cuando está abierta. La cuad: A rooftop, when it's open. The grid and the cathedral from above.
text.El bar del hostal. Ron barato y el previ: The hostel bar. Cheap rum and the pre-party before the beach bus. Earplugs if you sleep upstairs.
text.Patrimonio. Sube al techo: cal blanca, v: Heritage site. Climb to the roof: white lime, volcanoes and the bells. Rubén Darío is inside. The ticket is for the terrace.
Go early. The photo is the roof.
text.La plaza de la catedral. Leones, vendedo: The cathedral plaza. Lions, vendors and a bench in the shade. This is where you get your bearings.
text.El cono negro joven. Subes con tabla y b: The young black cone. You climb with a board and come down over the ash. Half a day from any hostel. Clothes you can throw away.
text.La luz de la tarde es mejor. Lleva un pa: The afternoon light is better. Bring a bandana for the dust.
text.Cráter activo y atardecer. Más largo que: Active crater and sunset. Longer than Cerro Negro. Book with someone who brings water and a flashlight.
text.La iglesia barroca amarilla. Fachada tal: The yellow baroque church. Carved facade, a short stop between parks.
text.Fundación Ortíz Gurdián. Dos casonas y u: Fundación Ortíz Gurdián. Two mansions and a real collection: painting and sculpture. The indoor break when León burns.
text.La parroquia indígena al oeste de la cua: The indigenous parish west of the grid. San Juan Bautista. Another León, different from the park.
text.El escritorio del hostal. Sandboard, Tel: The hostel's desk. Sandboarding, Telica and the shuttle to Peñitas. The usual booking.
text.Escritorios independientes cerca del par: Independent counters near the park. Compare the Cerro Negro price with Bigfoot before paying.
text.Bicis en los hostales. La cuadrícula col: Bikes at the hostels. The colonial grid is best seen by bike. Lock it up in the park.
text.Del mercado al mar: From the market to the sea
text.Bus del mercado a Poneloya y Peñitas. Ba: Bus from the market to Poneloya and Peñitas. Cheap, slow and local. Take a taxi if you carry boards.
text.Para llenar la casa. Agua, pollo, cervez: To stock the house. Water, chicken, beer. Fruit is still better at the market.
text.El súper más amplio. Importados cuando e: The bigger supermarket. Imports when Palí doesn't have them.
text.El mercado de la ciudad. De aquí salen l: The city market. Beach buses leave from here. Fruit, meat and plastic chairs.
text.La cadena nacional en León. Después del: The national chain in León. After the volcano, for sun and dust relief.
text.Mostrador independiente cerca de la cate: Independent counter near the cathedral. Cash and generics.
text.Casona grande, piscina y cuartos de casa: Big mansion, a pool and homey rooms. A few blocks from the cathedral.
text.Hotel pequeño, cuartos cumplidos y desay: Small hotel, decent rooms and breakfast. The middle ground when El Convento is full.
text.Eco lodge sobre la arena en la Isla Los: Eco lodge on the sand on Isla Los Brasiles, reached by a short boat ride from Poneloya. Cabins and dorms, surf and turtles in season. Sleep on the beach, not in the heat of downtown.
text.Cabañas y cocina italiana en la playa. E: Cabins and Italian cooking on the beach. You watch the sunset from your table.
text.Casa colonial remodelada que se alquila: Remodeled colonial house rented whole for up to 7 people: three bedrooms, a pool with hammocks and an equipped kitchen, in a good neighborhood. Rated 4.86 on Airbnb.
text.Hostal muy premiado del centro (se prese: Award-winning downtown hostel (it bills itself as the best in Nicaragua three years running), with a pool and a rooftop terrace. It has a second location, Poco a Poco Junior, and its own tour agency, Hola Hola Tours.
text.Hotel de cadena junto a la iglesia de La: Chain hotel next to La Recolección church, a few blocks from the cathedral. 50 rooms with A/C, a gym, a restaurant with a bar and parking; from about US$80.
text.Hostal frente al mar en Las Peñitas, al: Beachfront hostel in Las Peñitas, next to the Isla Juan Venado reserve, with a beach bar and restaurant, surf lessons and daily yoga. Beds from about US$13.
text.Hotel boutique dos cuadras al oeste del: Boutique hotel two blocks west of Parque San Juan, with a pool, a patio with plants, breakfast and parking. From about US$55.
text.Hostal social solo para adultos en el ce: Social, adults-only hostel downtown, with free breakfast and A/C at night. Designed for meeting people without losing sleep.
text.Hotel boutique de diez cuartos dos cuadr: Ten-room boutique hotel two and a half blocks north of the cathedral, with a courtyard pool and a restaurant serving healthy and international food. From about US$85.
text.Hotel boutique pequeño frente al mar en: Small boutique hotel on the waterfront in Las Peñitas: four rooms, a pool, a rancho and hammocks. From about US$80.
text.Hotel y restaurante en Las Peñitas, fren: Hotel and restaurant in Las Peñitas, facing the Isla Juan Venado reserve and steps from the beach. From dorms to family bungalows, with a spa, free bikes and breakfast; from about US$30.
text.Casa de huéspedes en una casona del cent: Guesthouse in a downtown mansion, two blocks west of Iglesia Zaragoza, with a pool and a garden. Rooms from US$24 to US$52, most with breakfast.
text.Lodge rústico de siete suites directamen: Rustic lodge with seven suites right on the sand in Las Peñitas, facing a good wave and with a covered pool that opens onto the beach. Each suite is booked on Airbnb (one is a treehouse for ten) or you can rent the whole lodge.
text.Hostal pequeño en el barrio El Sagrario,: Small hostel in barrio El Sagrario, near the cathedral, with dorms and private rooms from US$13 to US$28.
text.Hostal de los de siempre en una casa nic: A hostel of the classic kind in a Nica house downtown, with a patio and hammocks. Rated 8.5 on Hostelworld.
text.Hotel frente al mar entre Las Peñitas y: Beachfront hotel between Las Peñitas and Poneloya, with a pool, a seafood and grill restaurant, and a wave to surf out front. Rooms for one to five people; from about US$60.
text.Pan, quiche y café. El mostrador francés: Bread, quiche and coffee. The French counter León names for breakfast.
text.Un jardín escondido, plato y trago. La c: A hidden garden, a plate and a drink. Dinner away from the park.
text.Hummus, pita y ensalada cuando el calor: Hummus, pita and salad when the heat won't let you eat meat. Downtown.
text.Batidos y bowls. El cuarto sano después: Smoothies and bowls. The healthy room after Cerro Negro.
text.Parrilla en la playa. Pescado, cerveza f: Grill on the beach. Fish, cold beer and the Sunday table after a swim.
text.Bar de playa en Peñitas. Tacos, un cócte: Beach bar in Peñitas. Tacos, a cocktail and sand on the floor.
text.Un bar de León que siguen usando los est: A León bar students still use. Cheaper than the terraces on the park.
text.Cuando Via Via cierra la cocina, la noch: When Via Via closes the kitchen, the night continues here. Check the door: in León the night moves around.
text.En el parque. Guías que pelearon y una a: On the park. Guides who fought in the war and a rooftop over the cathedral. One hour, a tip and 1979.
Tip the guide. The view is the roof.
text.Al final de la calle: At the end of the street
text.La iglesia de color al final del eje est: The colorful church at the end of the east axis. A photo and a short stop on the walk.
text.El primer León, enterrado y desenterrado: The first León, buried and unburied by the lake, under Momotombo. Half a day. Ruins, not the living city.
text.La casa del ron en Chichigalpa, un viaje: The rum house in Chichigalpa, a trip from León. Distillery tour and tasting. The shuttle is booked downtown.
text.Guías sin fines de lucro. Telica, Cerro: Nonprofit guides. Telica, Cerro Negro and multi-day routes. The money goes to projects with children. Book a day ahead.
text.Carretilla y cajas de agua. La compra de: Cart and cases of water. The weekly shop for a house.
text.Mostrador en el barrio viejo. Genéricos,: Counter in the old neighborhood. Generics, cash and faster than the park.
text.Abierta 7:00–21:00. Vista a la bahía, ca: Open 7:00–21:00. Bay view, loungers, a cabana and a bar. The sunset drink is taken on the terrace.
text.Caminadoras, bicicletas, elípticas y pes: Treadmills, bikes, ellipticals and weights. Group yoga and a trainer on request. Peloton bikes in the gym.
text.Wifi de fibra, aire acondicionado y mesa: Fiber wifi, air conditioning and tables overlooking the pool and the bay. The room for working.
text.Sala con vista al mar y menú del club. E: A lounge with an ocean view and the club menu. The meeting point of La Santa María.
text.Bocados y batidos en la barra. Lo que ha: Bites and smoothies at the bar. What there is between the pool and the gym.
text.Básquet, pickleball y cornhole en el jar: Basketball, pickleball and cornhole in the garden.
text.Juegos de barco pirata, con fuerte, colu: Pirate-ship play area with a fort, swings and a slide. Lawn for kids to run on.
Tours, transfers, reservations and wellness. Gated entrance with security all day.
text.Pizza de horno de leña, todo lo que pued: Wood-fired pizza, all you can eat, open to everyone, not just guests.
text.Shuttle del hostal, según el cartel de l: Hostel shuttle, per this week's poster: Maderas, Remanso, Yankee, Escameca. 8:00–16:00.
text.La bahía se pone cobre. Un trago en la a: The bay turns copper. A drink on the sand, and then you decide the night.
text.Entre semana: cócteles 2x1 y cervezas a: Weekdays: 2x1 cocktails and half-price beers under the palapa. Quieter than the weekend band.
text.Piscina, patio y cócteles. Una cuadra al: Pool, patio and cocktails. One block west of the UNO.
text.La mesa de recuperación después del Sund: The recovery table after Sunday Funday. On the water, easy plates, no rush.
text.3C's Bakery, masajes y manicure junto a: 3C's Bakery, massages and manicures by the pool. 17:00–20:00.
text.Noche de alitas junto a la piscina. El h: Wing night by the pool. Happy hour continues from 15:00 to 19:00.
text.Pizza de horno de leña y cócteles. Entra: Wood-fired pizza and cocktails. Open to non-guests too.
text.El miércoles el happy hour es todo el dí: On Wednesdays happy hour lasts all day. Rum, vodka and tequila at C$50; cocktail of the day 2x1. 18+.
A midweek table on the water. The other Wednesday-night option if TreeCasa is too far.
text.Micrófono abierto del hostal. Detrás de: The hostel's open mic. Behind the church, one block south.
Karaoke on Thursdays, on the water.
text.Recorrido del jueves, sale del hostal. Q: Thursday's route, leaves from the hostel. Meet at Pachamama at 19:00.
text.Cafetería de día. El jueves el cuarto se: A cafeteria by day. On Thursdays the room becomes a bar.
text.Banda en vivo bajo la palapa, de viernes: Live band under the palapa, Friday through Sunday. No cover.
text.Banda de la casa en el camino a la playa: The house band on the road to the beach. Seafood, two pool tables, no cover.
text.Torneo del viernes. A veces el premio so: Friday tournament. Sometimes the prize is Sunday Funday tickets.
text.El cuarto tarde, al norte de la playa. S: The late-night spot, north of the beach. Weekends only.
text.Mural de galaxia en Paseo del Rey. Cover: Galaxy mural on Paseo del Rey. Cover on crawl nights; otherwise you walk right in.
text.Nueva ubicación: Rancho 1, la heladería: New location: Rancho 1, the ice cream shop on the beach (oceanfront), San Juan del Sur. Every Saturday 8:30–12:00. Vegetables, cheese, nacatamales, Ka Nuk, coffee and crafts.
text.Rancho 1 · heladería en la playa: Rancho 1 · ice cream shop on the beach
text.Quiz del sábado, antes del Sunday Funday: Saturday quiz, before Sunday Funday. In teams; the prize is almost always a drink.
text.Salsa, cumbia, merengue y bachata en viv: Live salsa, cumbia, merengue and bachata, on the sand.
text.Set en vivo del sábado en el pueblo. Pou: Saturday live set in town. Poutine, Caesars and the room that closes late.
text.Comer, nadar y tomar. Happy hour 15:00–1: Eat, swim and drink. Happy hour 15:00–17:00.
text.Recorrido de piscinas, domingo desde las: Pool crawl, Sunday from 13:00. Check-in at Pachamama, a stop at Social and the finale at Arribas, on the water.
text.Aquí cae el Sunday Funday. Frente al mar: This is where Sunday Funday lands. On the water, loud, the last stop.
text.La cúpula con luz de mañana. Sube si est: The dome in morning light. Go up if they're selling tickets.
text.Mesas en las piedras y la catedral al fo: Tables on the stones and the cathedral behind. Start here and turn off when the volume rises.
text.Cuando la Calzada se vacía, la noche sig: When the Calzada empties out, the night continues here.
text.Techo blanco y volcanes al horizonte. El: White roof and volcanoes on the horizon. The ticket is for the terrace.
text.El patio que se llena después de las nue: The courtyard that fills up after nine. A band when there is one.
text.Lun 21 · almuerzo especial, listo al med: Mon 21 · special lunch, ready at noon
text.Casa camino a Rivas: House on the road to Rivas
text.Chocolatería y cafetería. Variedad de ch: Chocolate shop and café. A variety of organic Nicaraguan chocolates and coffees, natural smoothies and other hot and cold drinks, a variety of delicious desserts, whole or sliced cakes, healthy vegan products, artisan baguette sandwiches and more...
text.Casa para renta a corto o largo plazo, e: House for short or long-term rent, modern style, spacious, 3 bedrooms for 8 people, a 5-minute walk from downtown and the beach, beautiful views over the sea, the town and the countryside, 2 covered terraces, A/C, jacuzzi...
text.Prueba el chocolate caliente o el browni: Try the hot chocolate or the brownie with ice cream. Vegan desserts are marked in the display case. WhatsApp +505 8764 0989.
text.Gimnasio moderno, limpio y abierto los 7: A modern, clean gym open 7 days a week on Paseo del Rey, where Crazy Crab used to be (20 m north of Hotel Anamar). Machines, Olympic bars, spin bikes, group classes and personal training.
text.Pase del día US$5, semana US$20, mes US$: Day pass US$5, week US$20, month US$30 (paying in person). WhatsApp +505 8553 3296.
text.El gimnasio más grande del pueblo, 1.5 c: The biggest gym in town, 1.5 blocks east of the market. Free weights, machines, a boxing ring and mats, with boxing, CrossFit, MMA and jiu-jitsu classes.
text.☎ 2568-2192. Clases privadas de boxeo co: ☎ 2568-2192. Private boxing lessons with Carlos. Instagram @fightclubgym_sjds.
text.Pesas al final de la playa: Weights at the end of the beach
text.Gimnasio pequeño y bien equipado en el e: A small, well-equipped gym at the north end of the beach, on Paseo del Rey. Plenty of machines and free weights at a good price. No air conditioning; closed at midday and on Sundays.
text.Pase del día aprox. C$180. Lleva toalla:: Day pass about C$180. Bring a towel: it is required to get in.
text.MMA, muay thai, BJJ y boxeo: MMA, Muay Thai, BJJ and boxing
text.Gimnasio de artes marciales desde 2008,: A martial arts gym since 2008, upstairs above Dockside at the port. Group and private BJJ, MMA, Muay Thai and boxing classes for all levels, with gloves, heavy bags and a weight rack.
text.Clase US$6, día US$10, mes US$40, sin co: Class US$6, day US$10, month US$40, no contract. Pay downstairs at Dockside. WhatsApp +505 8485 3176.
text.A 200 m de la playa, en el centro: 200 m from the beach, right downtown
text.A solo 200 metros de la playa y en pleno: Just 200 meters from the beach, right in the center of San Juan del Sur. A fully equipped apartment: queen bed plus sofa bed, full kitchen with microwave, fridge and coffee maker, and WiFi included. Food and drinks are allowed. Comfortable, private and safe; ideal for couples.
text.Centro · costado sur de la iglesia: Downtown · south side of the church
text.Contiguo a la antigua biblioteca, costad: Next to the old library, on the south side of the church. WhatsApp +505 8816 7161 (Yanaisy Ércia).
